mainTopic: What a גט may be written on: a cow's horn, living things and food, things attached to the ground, and a perforated pot
overview: The גמרא first asks why a husband who wrote a גט on a cow's horn can't just cut the horn off and give it. It answers from the פסוק "וכתב... ונתן": a גט may need only writing and giving, with no cutting in between. It then brings a ברייתא as the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule that a גט may not be written on something alive or on food. The רבנן read the word "ספר" as being about the גט's content instead. The גמרא then shows how each side learns the rules that a גט must be written (not money) and must make a complete break. A new משנה follows: a גט should not be written on something attached to the ground, but after the fact it can be valid if it was detached in time. The same משנה brings a dispute about erased paper and unfinished leather. שמואל, רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן explain the משנה as a case where the תורף was written after detaching, following רבי אלעזר. ריש לקיש explains it as being about the witnesses' signing, following רבי מאיר. Finally, a גט on the clay of a perforated pot is valid, and אביי and רבא argue about a גט on a leaf growing in such a pot, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not cut off the cow's horn?
steps.stepSummary: The slave's hand obviously can't be cut off, so the husband gives her the slave. But a cow's horn could be cut off, so why must he give her the whole cow?
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave's hand can't be cut off. But a cow's horn? Let him cut it off and give it to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה, which says that if the גט was written on a cow's horn the husband gives her the whole cow. It asks why he can't simply cut off the horn and give her only that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a slave, cutting off the hand is plainly forbidden, so giving the whole slave makes sense. A cow's horn can be removed with no such problem. So the משנה's ruling for the cow looks unnecessary.

To cut it off
A cow's horn

phrases.english: It is not possible to cut it off,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קֶרֶן שֶׁל פָּרָה לִיקְצְיַיהּ וְלִיתְּבַהּ לָהּ

steps.title: A גט may need only writing and giving
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "וכתב... ונתן": a valid גט is something that needs only writing and giving. A horn still attached needs cutting too, so it doesn't qualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And he writes... and gives it to her." A valid גט is something that lacks only writing and giving. That excludes this horn, which lacks writing, cutting, and giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah describes a גט as needing only two actions, writing and giving. A horn on a live cow would need a third action, cutting, so it can't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that cutting is forbidden. The פסוק describes a גט that needs only writing and then giving. A horn that would still have to be cut off between those two steps does not fit, so the husband must give her the whole cow with the writing on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking, still needing (an action)
Writing and giving
Cutting off
This is excluded

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the horn is a problem because cutting it is forbidden or hard. The only issue is the extra step between writing and giving.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a rule: a finished גט must be something he can hand over right away, with no extra step of cutting in between writing and giving.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And he writes" – "and gives it to her,"
something that is not lacking
anything except writing and giving;
excluding this, which is lacking
writing, cutting, and giving.

steps.terutzMaskana: A גט needing cutting after writing is invalid, so the whole cow must be given

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי's view from the משנה (no גט on something alive or on food) and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, etc. What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה, רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion, and asks where it comes from. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי הגלילי disallows writing a גט on anything alive or on food, while the רבנן allow it. The גמרא wants the source for his limits.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי

steps.title: The ברייתא: like a ספר, not alive and not food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "וכתב לה" that a גט may be written on anything, but the word "ספר" limits this to things that, like a scroll, are not alive and not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: "A scroll." I would know only that a scroll is valid. From where do we include any object? The verse says "and he writes for her": on anything. If so, why does it say "scroll"? Just as a scroll is not alive and is not food, so too any object that is not alive and is not food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads two words of the פסוק together. One word widens the materials allowed for a גט, and the other narrows them back down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ספר" alone would allow only a scroll. "וכתב לה" widens this to any material. The word "ספר" still teaches something: the allowed materials must be like a scroll, which is not alive and not food. That excludes a slave's hand and a cow's horn.

keyTerms.meaning: Scroll, document
From where do we include?
The פסוק teaches
In any case, on anything
Life, being alive

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic pattern of a general word (anything) limited by a specific example (like a scroll). It is the full source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא סֵפֶר אֵין לִי אֶלָּא סֵפֶר

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "וכתב לה" allows any material, but "ספר" limits it to things that, like a scroll, are not alive and not food

steps.title: The רבנן: ספר means the content, not the material
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that if the פסוק said "בספר" (in a scroll), it would be about the material. Since it says "ספר", it means the גט must contain a statement of the matter (ספירת דברים).
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If it were written "in a scroll," it would be as you said. Now that it is written "scroll," it comes to teach about an account of matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן, who allow a גט on living things and food, read the word "ספר". They read it as being about what the גט says, not what it is written on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "בספר" (in a scroll) would describe the surface the גט is written on, and then רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading would work. The פסוק says just "ספר", which the רבנן connect to ספירה, telling or recounting. So the word teaches that the גט needs the proper wording, and nothing limits the material.

keyTerms.meaning: And the רבנן (how do they read it)?
In a scroll
As you said
Now that it is written
An account or statement of the matters, the content of the גט

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads "ספר" as the material (like a scroll: not alive, not food). The רבנן read it as the content (ספירת דברים), so for them a גט may be written on anything, as long as it doesn't need cutting after the writing.
steps.confusionAlert: The whole argument rests on one letter: "בספר" would mean the material, but "ספר" without the ב means the wording of the גט.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how the רבנן, who argue with רבי יוסי הגלילי, read the word "ספר".

phrases.english: If it were written "in a scroll,"
it would be as you said;
now that it is written "scroll,"

phrases.notes: Playing on the word: ספר sounds like ספירה, telling or recounting, so it's about what the גט says.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אִי כְּתִיב בְּסֵפֶר כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's different reading of the word used in the ברייתא of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word: ספר means content, not material
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "ספר" limits the material of a גט, as רבי יוסי הגלילי holds
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, "ספר" requires proper content (ספירת דברים), so a גט may be written on living things or food
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute depends on whether "ספר" describes the material or the content of the גט

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from the word וכתב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the word וכתב, since they did not use it to allow a גט on anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word 'and he writes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what the רבנן learn from the word וכתב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי הגלילי used וכתב to teach that a גט can be written on anything, and ספר to limit that. The רבנן used ספר for a different idea, ספירת דברים. So the גמרא wants to know what job וכתב does for them, since every word in the תורה must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view arguing with רבי יוסי הגלילי
What do they do with it? (what do they learn from this word?)
'And he writes' (from the פסוק about divorce)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this word 'and he writes'
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי וְכָתַב מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the רבנן used ספר for another idea, the גמרא asks what they learn from וכתב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from the word וכתב.

steps.title: A woman is divorced only by writing, not by money
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use וכתב to teach that divorce works only through a written document. Without it, we might have compared divorce to קידושין, which can be done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to teach: she is divorced through writing, and not through money. You might have thought to compare leaving a marriage to entering it: just as entering a marriage can be done with money, so too leaving can be done with money. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן need וכתב to teach that a גט must be a written document. Money cannot end a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known היקש (comparison) between getting married and getting divorced. Since קידושין can be done with כסף, we might think divorce can be too. The word וכתב shows that divorce needs writing only.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (for a different lesson)
A comparison the תורה makes between two topics
Leaving a marriage (divorce)
Becoming married (קידושין)
You might have thought to say
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבי יוסי הגלילי's lesson from וכתב. For him it means 'write on anything'. For the רבנן it means 'only writing works, not money'.

phrases.english: They need it to teach
'Through writing she is divorced,
and she is not divorced through money'
For it would have entered your mind to say,
I will compare leaving a marriage to becoming married:
just as becoming married can be done with money,
so too leaving can also be done with money;

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ בִּכְתִיבָה מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת, וְאֵינָהּ מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת בְּכֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use וכתב to teach that divorce works only through writing and not through money, which blocks the comparison to קידושין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source that a marriage cannot be ended by paying money. Only a written גט works.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns 'writing, not money' from ספר כריתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי הגלילי, who used וכתב for something else, learns the 'only writing' rule from ספר כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יוסי הגלילי, learns it from 'scroll of severance': a scroll cuts her off, and nothing else cuts her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers in one line: where does רבי יוסי הגלילי get the rule that only writing works? From the words ספר כריתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי already used וכתב for 'write on anything', so he needs another source for 'not with money'. He reads ספר כריתות as 'a ספר is what cuts the marriage', which leaves out anything else, like money.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
He derives it from
'Scroll of severance', the תורה's name for a גט
Cuts her off (ends the marriage)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי הגלילי. He used וכתב for 'write on anything', so where does he learn 'not with money'?

phrases.english: He derives it from 'scroll of severance':
a scroll cuts her off from him,
and nothing else cuts her off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִסֵּפֶר כְּרִיתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבנן's source for 'writing, not money', the גמרא finds רבי יוסי הגלילי's source for the same rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from ספר כריתות that only a written document ends the marriage.

steps.title: The רבנן use ספר כריתות to require a full break
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need ספר כריתות to teach that a גט must completely cut the connection between husband and wife. A ברייתא shows that a condition binding her forever ruins the גט, but a time-limited condition is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side, the רבנן, need it for 'something that cuts between him and her', as a ברייתא teaches: 'Here is your גט on condition that you never drink wine', or 'on condition that you never go to your father's house'. If he says 'forever', that is not cutting off. If he says 'for thirty days', that is cutting off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the רבנן learn from ספר כריתות: a גט must make a complete break. It brings a ברייתא about conditions to show what that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition that ties the wife to her husband's wishes forever means the connection was never really cut, so the גט is not valid. A condition that lasts only a limited time, like thirty days, still lets the tie end completely, so the גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that cuts between him and her (a complete break)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
On condition that
Forever
Severance, a full cutting off

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule that a גט cannot carry a condition that keeps the wife bound to her husband forever.

phrases.english: And the other side?
phrases.notes: Now 'the other' means the רבנן, who used ספר כריתות for something else.

phrases.english: They need it for 'a thing that cuts between him and her',

'Here is your גט

phrases.notes: 'Forever' goes on both conditions: never drinking wine, or never visiting her father.

phrases.english: If he says 'for thirty days', that is cutting off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ דָּבָר הַכּוֹרֵת בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the רבנן learn from ספר כריתות instead, since they already learned 'writing, not money' from וכתב (step 7).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use ספר כריתות to teach that a גט must make a complete break, so a never-ending condition ruins it.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the full-break rule from the longer word
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the 'complete break' rule from the fact that the תורה wrote the longer word כריתות instead of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יוסי הגלילי, learns it from the change of כרת to כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי יוסי הגלילי gets the 'complete break' rule. The extra letters in the word כריתות teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have written the shorter word כרת. Writing the longer כריתות adds a second lesson, so רבי יוסי הגלילי gets both rules from one phrase: 'only writing' and 'a full break'. Now both sides have a source for every rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The shorter word for 'cut'

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the rules: a גט must be in writing (not money) and must fully end the tie. They only argue about which word teaches which rule. The רבנן use וכתב and ספר כריתות. רבי יוסי הגלילי uses ספר כריתות and the extra letters of כריתות.

phrases.english: And the other one?
He learns it from the change of 'כרת' to 'כריתות'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ מִכָּרֵת כְּרִיתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי הגלילי a source for the full-break rule that the רבנן learned in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי derives the full-break rule from the longer form כריתות instead of כרת.

steps.title: The רבנן do not learn from the longer word כריתות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not draw any lesson from the תורה writing כריתות instead of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side, the רבנן? They do not expound the difference between כרת and כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the extra letters in כריתות, which רבי יוסי הגלילי used in Step 10. The answer is that they simply do not learn anything from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, רבי יוסי הגלילי learned the 'complete break' rule from the longer word כריתות. The רבנן already learned that rule from the phrase ספר כריתות itself (Step 9), so they have no need for the longer form. They do not treat כרת versus כריתות as a source for any lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other side of the argument
They do not expound, meaning they learn no lesson from it
The short form of the word for 'cutting'

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a גט must completely cut the connection between husband and wife. They only disagree about which words in the פסוק teach this.

phrases.notes: He means the רבנן: what do they do with the longer word כריתות?

phrases.english: They do not expound 'כרת' versus 'כריתות'.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They learn nothing from it; they do not expound the כרת/כריתות difference.

steps.title: משנה: Writing a גט on something attached to the ground
steps.stepSummary: One should not write a גט on something attached to the ground. If he did and then detached it, signed it and gave it, it is valid. רבי יהודה invalidates it unless both writing and signing were done when it was already detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not write a גט on something attached to the ground. If he wrote it on something attached, then detached it, signed it and gave it to her, it is valid. רבי יהודה says it is invalid unless both the writing and the signing were done on something detached.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the rule about writing a גט on something still connected to the ground, and records רבי יהודה's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says that after the fact the גט is valid if it was detached before it was 'signed' and given. רבי יהודה is stricter and requires both the writing and the signing to be done on a detached item. This sets up the גמרא's question about how the משנה can forbid writing on something attached and then call it valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Attached to the ground, such as a growing plant
Detached, no longer connected to the ground
He detached it
Invalidates

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may not write a גט
on something attached to the ground.
If he wrote it on something attached,
then detached it, signed it, and gave it to her, it is valid.
רבי יהודה invalidates it,
unless its writing and its signing are done on something detached.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין כּוֹתְבִין בִּמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally a גט is not written on something attached. After the fact, if it was detached before signing and giving, it is valid. רבי יהודה requires both writing and signing on a detached item.

steps.title: משנה: Erased paper and unfinished leather
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא forbids writing a גט on erased paper or unfinished leather because the writing can be forged. The חכמים allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: One may not write a גט on erased paper or on unfinished leather, because it can be forged. And the חכמים say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second dispute about what material a גט may be written on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירא worries that on these surfaces someone could erase and change the writing without anyone noticing. The חכמים disagree and say a גט written on them is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Erased paper, paper that was written on and then erased
Unfinished, partly processed leather
To be forged or changed
They declare it valid

phrases.english: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין לֹא עַל הַנְּיָיר הַמָּחוּק
phrases.english: One may not write a גט on erased paper
nor on unfinished leather,
because it can be forged.
And the חכמים say it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second dispute in the same משנה about what a גט may be written on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בתירא forbids erased paper and unfinished leather out of fear of forgery. The חכמים allow them.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say a גט written on something attached is valid when it just said one may not write on something attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: He wrote it on something attached, and it is valid?! But you said in the first part, 'One may not write on something attached'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. The first line forbids writing on something attached, but the next line says such a גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If writing on an attached item is forbidden, it seems a גט written that way should not work. Yet the משנה calls it valid once it is detached and signed. The גמרא wants to know how both lines can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
But didn't you say?
The first part of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about רבי יהודה's view. The גמרא is pointing to a contradiction inside the תנא קמא's own words.

phrases.english: GEMARA: He wrote it on something attached, and it is valid?!
But you said in the first part, 'One may not write'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first part of the משנה in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a גט written on something attached is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first line forbids writing on something attached, so a גט written that way seems like it should be invalid.

steps.title: שמואל: He left a blank space for the key part
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the valid case is when the writer left blank the place for the תורף, the key personal part of the גט, and filled it in only after detaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה means a case where he left blank the place for the תורף.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל resolves the contradiction by narrowing the case where the משנה calls the גט valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden case is writing the whole גט on something attached. The valid case is when only the standard wording was written while attached, and the essential personal part was written after detaching. Since the part that makes the document this couple's גט was written on a detached item, the גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when, a phrase that limits the case
He left over, meaning he left blank
The essential, personal part of the גט, such as the names

steps.whatToRemember: A גט written on something attached is valid only if the תורף was left blank and written after the item was detached.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the תורף is the part of a גט that counts most, so the rules about how a גט is written apply mainly to it.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
This is only when he left blank the place for the תורף.
phrases.notes: The תורף is the personal part of the גט, like the names of the man and woman. He writes it after detaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁשִּׁיֵּיר מְקוֹם הַתּוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to call a גט fully written on something attached valid, which contradicts its first line.
steps.terutzMaskana: The valid case is only when the תורף was left blank and written after detaching. Writing the whole גט while attached is what the first line forbids.

steps.title: Two more Sages agree with שמואל's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא (quoted by רבי אלעזר) and רבי יוחנן (quoted by רבה בר בר חנה) both say the same thing as שמואל: the משנה is talking about a case where the place for the תורף was left blank.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said, quoting רבי אושעיא: this is a case where he left space for the key part. And רבה בר בר חנה also said, quoting רבי יוחנן: this is a case where he left space for the key part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל's answer from step 15 by showing that two other major Sages said exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new idea is added here. The point is that this answer is not one Sage's lone opinion. רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן also explain the משנה as a case where the תורף was written only after the material was detached.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too said: introduces another Sage who says the same thing
He left over, meaning he left a blank space
The place for the תורף, the personal key part of the גט (names, date)

phrases.english: And so too said Rabbi Elazar,
quoting Rabbi Oshaya:
And this is when he left space for the key part.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה,
phrases.english: And so too said Rabbah bar bar Chana,
quoting Rabbi Yochanan:
And this is when he left space for the key part –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds supporting traditions that match שמואל's answer in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן agree that the valid case in the משנה is when the place of the תורף was left blank and filled in after detaching.

steps.title: This answer follows רבי אלעזר, so the משנה is read with טופס and תורף
steps.stepSummary: The approach of שמואל and the others follows the תנא רבי אלעזר, who holds that the witnesses who see the handing over make the divorce work. So writing the תורף is what counts. The משנה is then read this way: do not write even the טופס on something attached, in case he writes the תורף that way too. But if he wrote only the טופס while it was attached, then detached it, wrote the תורף and gave it to her, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי אלעזר, who says the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce. And this is what the משנה means: one may not write the standard form, in case he writes the key part. If he wrote the standard form and then detached it, then wrote the key part and gave it to her, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names which תנא this answer follows and then rereads the whole משנה so that it fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, the signatures are not what makes the גט work, so the פסוק of 'and he shall write' is about the writing itself. That means the תורף must be written on detached material. The ban on writing even the טופס while attached is only a precaution, so after the fact the גט is valid as long as the תורף was written after detaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses who see the handing over are the ones who make the divorce take effect
The standard, general wording of a גט that is the same in every גט
And this is what it means: introduces a rereading of the source
He detached it from the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי אלעזר in 'ורבי אלעזר היא' is the תנא of the משנה era. He is not the אמורא רבי אלעזר who quoted רבי אושעיא a moment earlier.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how you explain the משנה depends on a basic question: what makes a גט work, the signing or the handing over.

phrases.english: And this follows Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא רבי אלעזר, not the רבי אלעזר who was just quoted.

phrases.english: who says: the witnesses of the handing over make the divorce.
And this is what it is saying:
One may not write the standard form
phrases.notes: He means on something attached to the ground.

phrases.english: lest he write the key part that way too.
If he wrote the standard form and then detached it,
then wrote the key part and gave it to her – it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: עֵדֵי מְסִירָה כָּרְתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds the answer of steps 15-16 in the view of a תנא and spells out the full reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה according to a specific תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say both that a גט may not be written on attached material and that one written that way is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי אלעזר, only the טופס was written while attached, as a forbidden precaution. The תורף was written after detaching, so the גט is valid.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the משנה means signing, following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees with the earlier reading. The משנה's word חתמו really means the witnesses signed it. The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that the signing witnesses make the divorce work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: we learned 'they signed it.' And this follows רבי מאיר, who says the signing witnesses make the divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different answer to the קשיא from step 14. He takes the word 'signed' in the משנה literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's approach had to read 'signed' as finishing the writing of the תורף. ריש לקיש says no, it means the witnesses' signatures. Since for רבי מאיר the signing is what makes the גט work, the תורה's requirement about detached material applies only to the signing.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses who sign are the ones who make the divorce take effect

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
We learned 'they signed it';
phrases.notes: He is pointing to the משנה's word וחתמו and saying it means the witnesses signed, not that the writing was finished.

phrases.english: and this follows Rabbi Meir,
who says the signing witnesses make the divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: חָתְמוּ שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a rival answer to the קשיא of step 14, instead of the answer of steps 15-17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reading of a word in the משנה and assigning it to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Signed' in the משנה could be read as filling in the תורף, as in שמואל's approach.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Signed' means the witnesses' signatures, and the משנה follows רבי מאיר's view that signing is what makes the גט work.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reading of the whole משנה
steps.stepSummary: Following ריש לקיש, the משנה means this. Do not write even the תורף on something attached, as a rabbinic decree in case the witnesses sign it while attached. But if he wrote the תורף while attached, then detached it, had it signed and gave it to her, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the משנה means: one may not write the key part, as a decree in case he has it signed. If he wrote the key part, detached it, had it signed and gave it to her, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the משנה reads line by line according to ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the תורה only requires that the signing be done on detached material. Writing even the תורף while attached is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה, so that people don't come to sign while attached. That is why, after the fact, the גט is valid if the signing happened after detaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Lest he have it signed (while still attached)
He had it signed by the witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the משנה. (1) שמואל, רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן follow רבי אלעזר (עדי מסירה כרתי): only the טופס was written while attached, and the תורף was written after detaching. (2) ריש לקיש follows רבי מאיר (עדי חתימה כרתי): even the תורף may be written while attached after the fact, as long as the signing came after detaching.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the shift. In step 17 the thing forbidden as a precaution is the טופס, out of concern for the תורף. Here the thing forbidden as a precaution is the תורף itself, out of concern for the signing.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
One may not write the key part,
as a decree, lest he have it signed that way.
If he wrote the key part, then detached it,
had it signed and gave it to her – it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין תּוֹרֶף, גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַחְתּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's answer by applying it to the full wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה into a rabbinic precaution and a Torah-level rule for validity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Do not write on attached material' and 'it is valid' seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on writing the תורף while attached is only a rabbinic גזירה. The Torah-level rule concerns the signing, so the גט is valid if it was signed after detaching.

steps.title: A גט written on the clay of a perforated pot is valid
steps.stepSummary: A גט written on the clay of an עציץ נקוב is כשר, because he can take the pot and give it to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote the גט on the clay of a pot with a hole in it, it is valid, because he can take the pot and give it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a new rule connected to the topic of writing a גט on something attached to the ground. Writing it on the clay of an עציץ נקוב works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עציץ נקוב counts as connected to the ground, so you might think it is like writing on the ground itself. But the pot can simply be lifted and handed over. So the husband can still give her the גט as it is, with nothing to cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: Clay, the material of an earthenware pot
A flower pot with a hole in the bottom, treated as connected to the ground
Valid
Attached to the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Being connected to the ground does not automatically make a גט פסול here. The point is that the pot can be picked up and handed over whole.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתָבוֹ עַל חֶרֶס שֶׁל עָצִיץ נָקוּב – כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: If he wrote it on the clay of a perforated pot, it is valid,
phrases.notes: A pot with a hole in the bottom draws from the ground, so it counts as attached to the ground.

phrases.english: because he takes it and gives it to her.
phrases.notes: "It" here means the whole pot, with the גט written on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתָבוֹ עַל חֶרֶס שֶׁל עָצִיץ נָקוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the readings of the משנה about writing on something attached, the גמרא moves to related cases of attached objects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written on the clay of an עציץ נקוב is כשר, since the pot itself can be given to her.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree about a leaf in a perforated pot
steps.stepSummary: If the גט is written on a leaf of a plant growing in an עציץ נקוב, אביי says it is כשר and רבא says it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote it on a leaf of a plant in a perforated pot: אביי says it is valid, and רבא says it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a harder case: the גט is written on a leaf growing in an עציץ נקוב. אביי and רבא argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the writing is on the plant, not on the pot. The leaf is still attached while it grows in a pot that counts as connected to the ground. אביי says כשר and רבא says פסול. Their reasons come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A leaf
Invalid

phrases.english: On a leaf of a perforated pot:
phrases.notes: He means a leaf of a plant growing in the pot.

phrases.english: Abaye says: it is valid,
and Rava says: it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל עָלֶה שֶׁל עָצִיץ נָקוּב אַבָּיֵי אָמַר כָּשֵׁר וְרָבָא אָמַר פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the pot itself (step 20) to a leaf growing in the pot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: אביי rules a גט on a leaf in an עציץ נקוב is כשר; רבא rules it is פסול.

steps.title: Starting to explain אביי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats "אביי says it is כשר" to begin explaining his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says it is valid —
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא repeats אביי's ruling so it can now explain why he holds that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeat is not a new ruling. It opens a clarification of each side of the dispute, starting with אביי. The actual reason comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached from the ground, the opposite of מחובר
The reasoning behind a ruling

phrases.english: Abaye says it is valid —

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates אביי's side of the dispute in step 21 in order to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of the explanation of why אביי holds that a גט on a leaf in an עציץ נקוב is כשר.
